hook.text: Casper shipped mattresses in boxes. Glossier built a beauty brand on Instagram. No retail stores needed.

buildup.text: Direct-to-consumer (DTC) brands sell through their own websites, bypassing retailers who take 40-60% margins.

discovery.text: Social media + e-commerce made DTC possible. You reach millions without paying for shelf space.

twist.text: Facebook ad costs tripled between 2019-2023. Rising customer acquisition costs squeezed DTC margins to nothing.

climax.text: Many DTC brands now open retail stores—the same channel they disrupted. Digital-only has limits.

punchline.text: Bypassed retail. Then opened stores. The revolution came full circle.

quiz.question: What forced many DTC brands to open physical stores?
options: Rising digital advertising costs made online-only unsustainable

details.summary: Direct-to-consumer brands bypass traditional retail channels to sell directly to customers, typically online. By owning the customer relationship and data, DTC brands achieve higher margins, faster feedback loops, and greater control over brand experience.
details.whyItMatters: DTC disrupted industries from eyewear to mattresses by cutting out retail markup and building direct relationships. Understanding this model shows how digital distribution enables new brands to compete against established retail incumbents.
takeaways: DTC brands sell directly to consumers, bypassing wholesale and retail intermediaries
Owning customer data enables personalized marketing and faster iteration
Rising customer acquisition costs challenge DTC profitability at scale

faq.question: What advantages do DTC brands have over traditional retail?
faq.answer: Higher margins from eliminating wholesale and retail markup, direct access to customer data and feedback, complete control over brand presentation and experience, and the ability to test products and messaging rapidly through digital channels.

faq.question: Why are many DTC brands now opening physical stores?
faq.answer: Online customer acquisition costs have risen dramatically. Physical stores serve as cost-effective marketing channels, provide product trial experiences, reduce return rates, and reach customers who prefer in-store shopping. The model is evolving toward omnichannel.
